messages:
Noah B: hi all, day 1 question: i'm behind a corporate firewall and want to run a quick streaming smoke test. should i use a sandbox key? also: can security whitelist a stable IP for my VM so i don't get blocked? worried about accidental 429 floods from my test harness.

Rae (DevEx): welcome Noah! :wave: Yes, use a sandbox key for local/dev tests. Hosted keys are for staging/prod. Sandbox keys have lower default quotas. Grab one at Console -> API Keys.

InfraBot: FYI sandbox defaults = 50 req/min and 6 concurrent streams per key. For larger tests request a temporary quota bump via an infra ticket.

Noah B: thanks. what's the fastest path to get traffic from a stable IP so security can whitelist?

Kiera - SRE: two quick options: 1) open an infra ticket to use the org devproxy forwarder (egress 34.201.99.11) — fastest for whitelist, or 2) spin a test VM in our dev VPC and run tests there. Devproxy is usually quicker.

Rae (DevEx): note: running the local docker devproxy still uses your laptop IP unless you have org-forwarder creds. Local run:
```
docker run -e RW_API_KEY=sandbox_XXX -p 8080:8080 redwood/devproxy:latest
# point your app at http://localhost:8080
```

Noah B: got it. any tips to avoid 429s when ramping? my harness fires lots of parallel streams.

Kiera - SRE: ramp gradually, use exponential backoff + jitter, honor Retry-After, and limit concurrency under the per-key stream cap. For CI, mint ephemeral keys per runner to spread load. If you need to simulate heavier traffic, include expected rps in the infra ticket.

Noah B: awesome. i'll try the docker devproxy to smoke test, then open an infra ticket if i need the org forwarder. can someone tag me once infra approves a temp bump? @Rae @Kiera

Rae (DevEx): will do 44d

Kiera - SRE: ping us in the ticket and we'll add you to the devproxy access group.
